azure.note: Default identity hue and the system interactive color: links, primary fills, focus, carets, list markers, field border. OKLCH approx: oklch(50% 0.185 258).

azure-deep.note: Hover/pressed partner; routine-dialog mark fill; .chip.azure ink.

azure-wash.note: Quiet 'you are here' background — default --h-wash: selected seat node, composer focus ring, assistant face. Card kinds are signaled by full wash, never a side stripe.

identity-line.note: Default --h-line: seat/entry face borders, .consult frame, .chip.azure border.

identity-teal.note: identity.ts quad: ink #0d6a68 / tile #0d7171 / wash #e3f1f0 / line #bfe0de. Answers 'which agent', never status.

identity-cyan.note: identity.ts quad: ink #0a66a3 / tile #0a6ba8 / wash #e2f0f9 / line #bedcf0.

identity-steel.note: identity.ts quad: ink #3f4a58 / tile #55606e / wash #edeff2 / line #d3d9e1.

ink-2.note: Secondary text. ink-3 (#5c6e82) is a near-identical third grade for labels/times/placeholders.

ink-3.note: Micro-labels, timestamps, placeholders, muted notes. Interchangeable with ink-2 in practice.

paper.note: App background, thread surface, board ground, composer field fill.

sheet.note: Raised surfaces: bench rail, bars, dialogs, rows, prov line, composer on focus.

tint.note: Hover fills, idle chips, tile faces, segmented track, team-card head band.

rule-2.note: Stronger hairline: composer box, dialog frame, dashed provisional edges, idle dots, team-card frame.

user-entry-wash.note: The soft band behind user entries — a full wash, not a bubble.

thread-rule-ink.note: The 1px line every 28px that rules the thread.

margin-rule-azure.note: The vertical spine 26px into the sheet body, faded at both ends.

scrim-rail-ink.note: Scrim behind the bench drawer and the activity overlay.

ran.note: RESERVED: a stored row recorded a finished action. Never on interactive affordances.

ran-wash.note: Pale partner of Ran Green; the .pulse.on glow ring.

waiting.note: RESERVED: blocked on a worker/tool/decision that does not exist here. Real pending only (realPending gate).

fault.note: RESERVED: failed, cancelled, never answered. Also the delete-confirm mark and danger ghost ink.

fault-wash.note: Pale partner of Fault Red; fault entry panel and danger ghost hover fill.

fault-line.note: Mid-tone border for .chip.fault and the fault entry panel.

danger-line.note: Resting border of the danger ghost button.

danger-line-hover.note: Hover border of the danger ghost button.

slate.note: The ONLY dark surface in the app, reserved for fenced model output.

slate-2.note: Frame and bar divider inside the code block.

code-bar.note: The code block's language/copy header strip.

code-lang.note: Uppercase 9.5px language tag; copy-btn in-slate tones #9db2ca resting, #2c3c4f border, #22303f fill, #3d5169 hover — all one-offs.

display.purpose: Manrope 800 h1 at 27px base; stepped to 22px identity bar, 20px sheet bar, 24px pane heads. Contrast carried by weight.

title.purpose: Manrope 700 h3 15px; model ### at 14px, model ## at 16px.

body.purpose: DM Sans 14px/1.6 UI default — everything not a heading, label, or measurement.

thread-text.purpose: Thread replies and composer at 15px (lh 1.7 / 1.55), hard 80ch measure (--measure). RichText re-typesets model markdown into React nodes here; list markers take --h-ink.

label.purpose: Uppercase 700 at 10–11px, tracking .05–.1em: group labels, board heads, chips, entry tags, field labels, pane-h2 counts.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, 9.5–12.5px, measurement only: stamps, counts, char/token figures, model ids, fault detail. Never prose.

fontLoading.name: self-hosted-next-font
fontLoading.value: DM_Sans -> --font-body, Manrope -> --font-display, JetBrains_Mono -> --font-mono (next/font/google, display: swap, applied in layout.tsx)
fontLoading.purpose: There is no remote Google @import; the literal family names in CSS stacks are fallbacks only.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Resting lift: composer box, active segmented pill (var(--shadow-sheet)).

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Raised-over-page state: dialogs, toasts, jump pill, board overlay, open drawer (var(--shadow-lift)).

shadows.name: button
shadows.purpose: 2px tint under azure primary fills only.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single system ease (var(--ease)); everything timed uses it.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: The one entrance settle: dialogs .26s, toasts .22s, jump pill .20s.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: The only loop: the 2px --h-ink streaming caret AND the In-flight row's caret-st dot — literally the same keyframe. Reduced-motion: rests at 60% opacity.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button hover/active 120ms color-and-press transitions; send adds scale(.97).

motion.name: field-shift
motion.purpose: Composer box border/background/shadow shift, entry-tools opacity reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) clamps all animation/transition durations to .01ms; .caret, .caret-st rest at opacity .6
motion.purpose: Global clamp already shipped; new motion must fall inside it.

layoutDimensions.name: measure
layoutDimensions.purpose: var(--measure): the thread/prose cap for entry text, prov line, consult cards, rich blocks.

layoutDimensions.name: gutter
layoutDimensions.purpose: var(--gutter): thread and composer horizontal rhythm (thread left padding is gutter+6).

layoutDimensions.name: thread-column
layoutDimensions.purpose: Max width of the thread inside the fluid centre column; panes cap at 980px.

layoutDimensions.name: depth-step
layoutDimensions.purpose: Per-level indent of seat nodes via --depth; org-chart rows indent 15px.

browserSurface.name: selection
browserSurface.purpose: Soft azure highlight. Recorded one-off, not a token.

browserSurface.name: caret
browserSurface.purpose: Azure text cursor in every field.

browserSurface.name: scrollbar
browserSurface.value: ::-webkit-scrollbar 11px; thumb #c3cfdd with 3px paper outline, radius 9px; hover #a8b9cc; transparent track
browserSurface.purpose: Paper-outlined channel, not a bar. The 9px thumb radius is a one-off.

browserSurface.name: focus-ring
browserSurface.value: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--h-ink); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
browserSurface.purpose: The only outline in the system, and it takes the LOCAL identity hue — focus reads 'this agent'. Never suppressed.

browserSurface.name: one-off-inks
browserSurface.value: #24303f user entry text · #6f2019 fault entry text · rgba(27,36,48,.055)/rgba(234,240,247,.6) entry fabrics · delete-dialog inline fault fill overrides
browserSurface.purpose: Single-use literals recorded so the detector does not read them as drift; promote to :root before reuse.

Nova7:39 PM
reasoning · verbatim from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7
The user wants a two-sentence description. Keep it plain and factual…

This workspace is a conversational assistant for named agents.

  1. Threads persist
  2. Claims are server rows
You7:38 PM
Put together the launch brief.

narrative.overview: The screen is a shift board, not a notebook. Three columns do three different jobs: the left rail is the organisation — teams rendered as reporting trees of seat nodes, each carrying who it reports to, what its stored rows say it is doing, its message count and its last touch — the centre gives the selected seat's thread real width at an 80ch measure on ruled paper with the reply's provenance printed inline directly beneath it, and the right column is an activity board that behaves like a printer: In flight, Needs attention, Upcoming, Record — every row is a stored run, delegation, audit event or approval, or a live fact this client itself received over SSE. The material world stays cool paper under white sheets, hairline rules, one azure doing all interactive work. What the Workbench adds is identity: each agent carries one of six cool hues answering 'which agent' and never 'what is happening'; status colors are reserved for states a stored row produced; monospace is reserved for measurement.
keyCharacteristics: Three named zones: organisation-as-navigation (left), the thread at an 80ch measure with inline provenance (centre), the activity printer that only prints recorded rows (right).
Identity hues mark who, semantics mark state, monospace marks measurement — three orthogonal systems that never bleed into each other.
Cool paper under white sheets, hairline rules, one azure for interactivity; the identity hue extends the 'you are here' wash per agent.
The thread sits on printed 28px rule lines with a faint azure margin spine; entries hang off it at 30px face tiles.
State is provenance: the last real reply carries one printed line — state pill, provider, model, chars, estimated tokens, saved-at — expandable into a plain-language note of exactly what happened.
Motion is one entrance settle (rise), one loop (the caret blink, shared by the streaming reply and the In-flight row), and 120ms press transitions, all clamped under prefers-reduced-motion.
Radii only 6/8/10px plus pills; the only dark surface in the app is the code block.
DM Sans body, Manrope headings, JetBrains Mono measurement — self-hosted through next/font, not remotely imported.

rules.name: The Who-Not-Status Rule
rules.body: An identity hue answers 'which agent' and nothing else. It never means busy, waiting, or done; those words belong exclusively to ran/waiting/fault. Conversely a state color never decorates an interactive affordance.

rules.name: The Recorded-State Rule
rules.body: A color state is a claim about the server. If the server did not record it, the element wears idle neutral and the copy says what is true. toneOf()'s sample parameter forcing idle is the law; new surfaces must pass the flag, not hand-pick tones.

rules.name: The Printer Rule
rules.body: The activity board prints rows. Every one is a stored run, delegation, audit event or approval — or a live SSE fact this client actually received — newest first, timestamped in mono. The live layer never rewrites the record.

rules.name: The No-Side-Accent Rule
rules.body: A card kind is signaled by a full wash (.consult on --h-wash, .entry-user on the entry wash), never by a colored border-left stripe. The 1px blockquote rule is typography, not an accent, and is the only left border in the system.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace means a number, a timestamp, an id, or a machine detail. Never set prose, a button label, or a heading in mono. If it isn't something you'd check with a ruler, it isn't mono.

rules.name: The Label Case Rule
rules.body: Micro-labels are uppercase with at least .05em tracking at 9.5-11px; nothing else in the system is letter-spaced upward.

rules.name: The Paper Stack Rule
rules.body: Depth is state, not hierarchy: a shadow appears when something is physically above the page (dialog open, overlay shown, drawer slid out, pill selected) and disappears when it settles back. Resting rows, nodes and thread entries are flat.

dos: Do treat globals.css :root as the single normative token source and src/lib/identity.ts as the single source of hues; new CSS references var(--paper) … var(--ease) and var(--h-*) inside agent-scoped subtrees.
Do keep fonts on the next/font path (--font-body / --font-display / --font-mono from layout.tsx); never add a remote @import.
Do reserve green/amber/red for statuses toneOf() produced from a real server row, always passing the sample flag; seeded rows render idle and say 'sample'.
Do print only recorded rows in the activity board — or live SSE facts this client received — each with a mono stamp and words explaining what it means; the live layer never rewrites the record.
Do use identity hues for 'who': selection washes, faces, focus, carets, live rows, consult cards, list markers. A status question never gets a hue answer.
Do print the reply's provenance as the one inline .prov line under the last real reply, with the honest note on open; never fabricate progress, replay stopped streams, or fill gaps.
Do render model text through RichText React nodes; reasoning arrives folded and labelled, never deleted; never inject model or user text as HTML.
Do keep monospace to measurement (<time>, counts, char/token figures, model ids) — the .num, time, .mono selector already enforces it for timestamps.
Do cap thread prose at the 80ch measure and let 28px rule lines, hairline dividers and the margin spine do the structural work instead of boxes.
Do use 6/8/10px radii and 99px pills only; 1px rule hairlines for separation; dashed borders only for provisional/unfiled things; non-creation stated in words, not dashed styling.
Do reuse .only-narrow / .only-wide for mode-specific chrome and the 1180px/860px collapse order (activity board to overlay, then bench to drawer).

Do keep motion to the recorded vocabulary (one rise settle, one blink loop, 120ms press, 140ms field shift, 240ms drawer) on var(--ease), inside the shipped prefers-reduced-motion clamp with carets resting at 60%.
Do let copy state boundaries as content ('No background worker: due work executes when this workspace is read', 'no browser, files, or connectors').
donts: Don't resurrect the discarded Bench Notebook devices: no taped evidence slips, no .slip cards, no printed .key state legend, no margin slip scroll-tie, no flat agent-tab index list, no ink-line composer. They are deleted from the code.
Don't reintroduce the retired warm-ivory/violet world: paper stays cool (#f4f7fa) and the only warm hue is the reserved waiting state.
Don't use state colors on interactive affordances or decorative dots, and don't use identity hues to mean status; each family answers exactly one question.
Don't mark sample or unconfigured things with ran green, live badges, or optimistic counts; keep the realPending gate on every new alert surface.
Don't signal a card kind with a colored border-left or any >1px side stripe; use the full wash (.consult on --h-wash). Side stripes are a detector AI tell this system refuses.
Don't set prose, headings or button labels in JetBrains Mono, and don't use it as an aesthetic tech font.
Don't add shadows beyond --shadow-sheet / --shadow-lift (plus the fixed azure-fill button tints), and don't shadow resting surfaces.
Don't add radii outside 6/8/10px/pill, razor corners, glassmorphism, or a second dark surface — the code block owns slate.
Don't add infinite animation beyond the caret blink (and its In-flight dot, which is literally the same keyframe), and don't animate anything not lifted, settled, or pressed.
Don't mint off-token hexes; single-use literals stay single-use. If one is needed twice, promote it to :root first.
Don't let the composer's right-hand line be static: token estimate while typing, 'Stop keeps what has arrived' while streaming, keyboard instruction only when idle and wide.
